To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
perfusion parameters are different in ischemic lesion and the contralateral hemisphere during the first 24 h after stroke.

perfusion CT parameters are significantly different between the lesion and contralaterally healthy hemisphere in the first 24 hours after stroke onset and that perfusion parameters associated to stroke severity and outcome are relevant for prescription of thrombolysis.
perfusion CT parameters are significantly different between the affected and unaffected hemisphere in the first 24 hours of acute ischemic stroke.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a possibility to use perfusion computed tomography (perfusion CT) in the early acute stroke phase for the evaluation of local cerebral hemodynamics.
the study of the perfusion CT parameters and the relationship with stroke severity and the outcome.
the dynamics of perfusion parameters in the early phase of ischemic infarct.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CT-perfusion can be a useful adjunctive method for the assessment of ischemic stroke patients.

perfusion CT in acute stroke patients provides additional information on local hemodynamic parameters and is helpful for the prescription of reperfussion therapy beyond the 3-4,5h "therapeuthic window" and for the prognosis.
CT-perfusion can be recommended for patients with suspected stroke, especially for those with unclear clinical symptoms, in the first hours after stroke.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CT-perfusion can be a valuable method in the acute phase of ischemia, allowing to evaluate the degree of tissue ischemia and the extent of ischemic penumbra, which can be used for prescription of thrombolytic therapy.
perfusion CT can be used to assess the extent of the ischemic penumbra and the core of the ischemic lesion in the acute phase.

the CT-perfusion parameters are useful in predicting stroke outcome, and can be used in clinical practice for individualized prescription of thrombolytic therapy in patients with acute ischemic stroke.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CT-perfusion allows the assessment of the severity of ischemic lesion in the early acute period and to predict the outcome of stroke.
perfusion CT parameters may be used for the prediction of stroke severity, prognosis and response to reperfusion therapy.

perfusion computed tomography (perfusion CT or PCT) allows us to evaluate brain perfution in the acute stage of stroke and provides additional information on local hemodynamic changes in the brain of patients with stroke.
